title: Private/VPC Deployments — PRD: Network, Upgrade, and Air-Gap Acceptance Criteria
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Several enterprise prospects require Private/VPC or fully air-gapped on-prem deployments of Redwood. This PRD captures the product requirements, constraints, and measurable acceptance criteria for networking, in-place and out-of-place upgrades, and air-gapped deployment patterns. Goals: (1) Define a secure, minimal network footprint that satisfies enterprise networking (private endpoints, explicit egress controls, DNS requirements); (2) Specify an upgrade strategy that works for VPC and air-gapped customers with predictable RTO/RPO and clear rollback paths; (3) Define what we support in air-gapped mode (package/image distribution, KMS integration patterns, telemetry options) and what is out-of-scope. Audience: PMs, Eng leads (runtime, infra, ops), Security, Solutions Engineering, and Sales engineering.
requirements: Private network: Support deployment where all control-plane and data-plane traffic can be pinned to customer VPC subnets and private endpoints (no public ingress).
Egress policy: Provide explicit list of optional egress endpoints and IP ranges for hosted-control-plane connectivity; support both zero-egress (air-gapped) and allowlisted-egress modes.
DNS: Allow customers to provide DNS entries or use an internal DNS overlay; runtime must resolve model files and internal services without internet DNS dependencies when air-gapped.

KMS: Support both cloud KMS integrations (AWS KMS/GCP KMS/Azure KeyVault) for VPC deployments and an HSM/KMS shim for air-gapped customers with local key material. Key rotation must be supported with no downtime.

Image & artifact distribution: Provide documented tooling and scripts for mirroring container images, model artifacts, and OS/security patches to an internal artifact registry; support checksum verification and signed artifacts.
Upgrade modes: Two supported upgrade modes: in-place orchestrated upgrade with automated rollback, and offline replace (out-of-place) upgrade that operators can run in air-gapped environments.

Telemetry and metrics: For air-gapped installs, provide an offline metric bundle export/import format and a self-hosted Prometheus + Grafana reference configuration. Optional metrics-forwarding to Redwood hosted console must be explicitly opt-in by customer.
Time sync & CA: Document NTP and CA requirements; provide a local CA bootstrap flow for air-gapped installs.
Auth & RBAC: Integrate with customer SSO where available; default must be local admin for air-gapped initial bootstrap.
Operator tooling: Provide CLI and runbook for upgrade, rollback, health-checks, and emergency data extraction.
acceptance_criteria: Network: Documented VPC architecture diagrams (public and private variants) and a validated test deployment in customer-style network that exercises private endpoints only (no public IPs).
Egress: When zero-egress mode is selected, deployment validates that no outbound packets to the public internet are observed during smoke tests and model loads.

Upgrade: Perform a staged canary upgrade in an infra sandbox: a) canary pod pool upgraded with no request error rate increase > 0.5% at P90 latency, b) full rollout completes within the documented window, c) agreed rollback script returns system to pre-upgrade state within target RTO (15 minutes for control-plane config changes, 60 minutes for full runtime image rollback).
Air-gapped image mirroring: Using provided mirror scripts, a new runtime image can be pulled into an internal registry and deployed without internet access; checksums and signatures are validated.
KMS: Encrypt/decrypt flows for secrets must succeed against local HSM shim; key rotation must occur with zero data loss in staged test.
Telemetry: Exported metrics bundle from air-gapped environment can be ingested by Redwood dev environment tooling for post-mortem analysis.
Auth: SSO integration test succeeds when customer SSO is available; in air-gapped bootstrap local admin access is verified.
Documentation: Ops runbook, network checklist, and upgrade playbook exist in Confluence and contain step-by-step commands and expected outputs.
non_functional_requirements: Downtime targets: For control-plane-only config changes target downtime = 0; for full runtime image replacement target P99 latency impact < 2x baseline during rolling upgrade.
RTO/RPO: Upgrade rollback RTO <= 60 minutes for runtime rollback; data RPO = 0 for persistent state (we do not expect data loss during supported upgrades).
Performance baseline: Private deployments must achieve within 15% of hosted tail-latency (P95) for identical hardware profiles.
Security: All artifacts signed; TLS mutual authentication enforced between internal services by default.
Audit logging: Admin actions (upgrades, key rotations) must be logged and exportable in a standard format.
scope_changes: Initial draft included automated remote patching of OS images for air-gapped sites — scope reduced: we will provide mirroring tooling and operator runbooks but not perform remote OS patch orchestration in 1.0.
Requested support for multi-cluster federation (single control plane across multiple air-gapped sites) deferred to a follow-up epic.
Decision: We will not require customers to open outbound TLS to third-party CDNs for production by default; mirror-based distribution is the supported pattern for air-gapped installs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): Build reference implementation in internal lab using representative VPC and air-gapped topology + run the full acceptance suite.
Phase 2 (pilot): Onboard two customers via Solutions Engineering; execute pre-flight network checklist and one dry-run upgrade.
Phase 3 (GA): Publish docs, mirror scripts, and operator CLI; offer pilot customers a guided upgrade for free in first 90 days.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misconfigure NAT/DNS causing failed downloads during mirror bootstrap. Mitigation: Provide a pre-flight network validation CLI and an exhaustive checklist.
Risk: Key rotation complexity in air-gapped HSM environments. Mitigation: Provide an HSM shim with automated rotation helpers and samples; require customer validation during pilot.

Risk: Upgrade rollback not tested on customer hardware. Mitigation: Include rollback scripts in install package and require pilot customers to run a dry-run in a staging environment before production upgrade.
